prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 4.21. Exact Sanskrit: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः ।
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ २१ ॥ Exact stored meaning: Without aspiration, with mind and self restrained, having abandoned all possessiveness — performing action only for the body's sake, he incurs no sin. Chapter context: Knowledge, action, teaching lineage, offering and insight. Depict the verse-specific symbolism; the iconic divine descent is appropriate only where stated. Distinguish the many kinds of offering without text labels. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, always contented, depending on nothing — even while being fully engaged in action, he truly does nothing at all. Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Content with whatever comes unsought, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, and equal in success and failure — even having acted, he is not bound. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.21: Without aspiration, with mind and self restrained, having abandoned all possessiveness — performing action only for the body's sake, he incurs no sin.
